import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Beal conjecture

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beal_conjecture)
-/

namespace BealConjecture

def bealConjecture : Prop := ∀ {A B C x y z : ℕ},
    A ≠ 0 → B ≠ 0 → C ≠ 0 → 2 < x → 2 < y → 2 < z →
    A^x + B^y = C^z → 1 < Finset.gcd {A, B, C} id

/--
The **Beal Conjecture**: if we are given positive integers $A, B, C, x, y, z$ such that
$x, y, z > 2$ and $A^x + B^y = C^z$ then $A, B, C$ have a common divisor.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem beal_conjecture : bealConjecture := by
  sorry

/--
The Beal Conjecture implies Fermat's last theorem
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem flt_of_beal_conjecture (H : bealConjecture) :
    FermatLastTheorem := by
  intro n hn x y z hx hy hz
  by_contra h
  apply mul_ne_zero (mul_ne_zero hx hy) hz
  by_contra H''
  obtain ⟨hx, hy, hz⟩ : x ≠ 0 ∧ y ≠ 0 ∧ z ≠ 0 := by aesop
  set G := Finset.gcd {x, y, z} id
  set x' := (x / G : ℕ)
  set y' := (y / G : ℕ)
  set z' := (z / G : ℕ)
  obtain ⟨hGx, hGy, hGz⟩ : G ∣ x ∧ G ∣ y ∧ G ∣ z := by
    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> apply Finset.gcd_dvd (by aesop)
  obtain ⟨hx', hy', hz'⟩ : x' ≠ 0 ∧ y' ≠ 0 ∧ z' ≠ 0 := by
    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩ <;>
      apply Nat.div_ne_zero_iff_of_dvd (by assumption) |>.mpr ⟨(by assumption), _⟩ <;> aesop
  have Hxyz' : x'^n + y'^n = z'^n := by
    rwa [Nat.div_pow hGx, Nat.div_pow hGy, Nat.div_pow hGz,
      ←Nat.add_div_of_dvd_right, Nat.div_left_inj (dvd_add _ _)]
    all_goals apply pow_dvd_pow_of_dvd ; assumption
  apply ne_of_lt <| H hx' hy' hz' hn hn hn Hxyz'
  rw [←Finset.gcd_div_id_eq_one (Finset.mem_insert_self x {y, z}) (by trivial),
    Finset.gcd_eq_gcd_image, Finset.image_insert, Finset.image_insert,
    Finset.image_singleton]

end BealConjecture

findings.description: The docstring at lines 32–33 concludes only that A, B, C “have a common divisor.” Literally, this requires nothing: 1 divides every triple. The Lean statement correctly requires `1 < Finset.gcd {A, B, C} id`; the omission is confined to the docstring.
findings.source_evidence: The opening statement of https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beal_conjecture says that positive integer solutions with x, y, z > 2 have “a common prime factor.” The “BEAL'S CONJECTURE” statement at https://www.bealconjecture.com/ uses the same wording.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace “have a common divisor” with “have a common prime factor” or “have a common divisor greater than 1.” No Lean statement change is needed.

reformulations.difference: Lean expresses the existence of a common prime factor by `1 < Finset.gcd {A, B, C} id`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The finite-set gcd equals `Nat.gcd A (Nat.gcd B C)`, including when bases repeat. Since A is nonzero, this gcd is positive. If it exceeds 1, a prime divisor of it divides all three bases. Conversely, a prime dividing all three bases divides their positive gcd, making that gcd at least the prime and hence greater than 1. The full equivalence between the Lean definition and the source's positive-integer/common-prime formulation was proved in `/workspace/review/scratch.lean`, without using the conjecture theorem.

sources_consulted: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beal_conjecture — opening formulations, related examples, relation to FLT, partial results, prize, and variants.
https://www.bealconjecture.com/ — “BEAL'S CONJECTURE” and the background discussion of reducing FLT solutions to coprime bases.

review.notes: All three declarations were verified; no mathematical misformalization was found. Wikipedia still records Beal's conjecture as unsolved. Mathlib's FLT definition matches the source, and `#print axioms` confirms that the file's conditional FLT proof does not depend on `sorryAx`. Scratch proofs and boundary tests compiled successfully. Enumeration for bases 1–16 and exponents 3–6 found 11 solutions, all with gcd greater than 1. Tests also checked repeated bases, zero/one gcd cases, and excluded exponent-2 examples. The linked AMS prize page returned HTTP 403; the cited Wikipedia article and Beal's website supplied the needed statements. The reviewed file was not modified.
